subject: Clarify IP exposure & limitation for EdgePilot pilot order
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <contracts@vectorlabs.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Marco Ruiz <procurement@vectorlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Initial order form redlines — IP/third-party indemnity concerns

Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the draft order form for our EdgePilot pilot. We've looped in procurement (Marco) below. Our GC flagged the indemnity section as currently overly broad for our pilot scope — specifically: (1) the third-party IP indemnity applies without a revenue/usage threshold; (2) defense control is unilateral; and (3) there's no cap tied to fees or an insurance/escrow mechanism.

For a time-limited pilot we need: a dollar cap equal to 12 months of fees for the pilot, mutual defense control for third-party claims arising from Vector data or outputs, and a carveout for pre-existing open-source claims. Can you review and confirm what Redwood can accept as a pilot compromise?

I've attached our short order form with the redlines (Vector_OrderForm_v1.pdf).

-Lydia
Senior Counsel, Vector Labs
attachments: Vector_OrderForm_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Lydia Chen <contracts@vectorlabs.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 12:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial order form redlines — IP/third-party indemnity concerns

Lydia — thanks and appreciate the clear asks. We're open to a pilot-specific compromise; below are the high level positions from legal and sales. Attaching our redline for clarity (Redwood_orderform_redline_20271208.pdf).

Summary of Redwood position (pilot only):
- Cap: Redwood can accept a cap equivalent to 12 months of paid fees for the pilot term (cap limited to amounts paid by Vector under the order form).
- Defense control: Redwood requests lead defense control for third-party IP claims with standard cooperation obligations; however we will agree to an approval right for Vector over any settlement that imposes obligations on Vector (money or injunctive relief).
- OSS carveout: Redwood will exclude claims arising solely from Vector's use of third-party open-source code that is not part of Redwood-managed model artifacts. We cannot carve out model-originated claims.
- Insurance/escrow: We do not require escrow for pilots; we can provide proof of Insurance upon request.

Open items we need from Vector:
1) Confirmation that the pilot is limited to the named accounts and usage volumes in the order form.
2) A short form statement that Vector will not incorporate Redwood outputs into a production-facing redistribution without separate agreement.

If those are acceptable, legal can produce a one-paragraph pilot-specific indemnity addendum. Jordan / Marissa: can you confirm risk tolerance on the defense-control language and settlement approval?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_orderform_redline_20271208.pdf (pdf)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 15:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial order form redlines — IP/third-party indemnity concerns

Kimberly / Marissa — quick note from commercial: approving the 12-month fee cap for pilot is fine. On defense control, sales prefers Redwood retain lead control to keep operational continuity (we have preferred counsel and playbooks). The settlement approval carveout for Vector makes sense — we should ensure it can't be used to veto reasonable operational settlements. 

Also flag: Vector asked earlier for an entitlement to sandbox exports post-pilot; if they get that right we should require a separate license and warranty/indemnity shift. Keep me posted on final wording so I can coordinate commercial approvals.

-Jordan

From: Lydia Chen <contracts@vectorlabs.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Marco Ruiz <procurement@vectorlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial order form redlines — IP/third-party indemnity concerns

Kimberly / team — thanks for the quick reply and the redline. A couple of clarifications from our side: 1) the cap tied to amounts "paid by Vector under the order form" — can it alternatively be "total fees invoiced for the pilot" to avoid disputes about credits/usage adjustments? 2) defense control — we can agree to a limited approval right for settlements but would like veto power over any settlement that could result in restrictions on our use of outputs (e.g. an injunction). 3) OSS carveout — we will provide a list of included OSS at signing for mutual acceptance.

If we can get alignment on those points, procurement can sign the pilot order and move to signature via DocuSign. We've included a preferred procurement contact here: Marco Ruiz.

Thanks,
Lydia

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Lydia Chen <contracts@vectorlabs.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial order form redlines — IP/third-party indemnity concerns

Lydia / Marco — appreciate the clarifications. Proposed final pilot compromise (we can incorporate as a 1-paragraph addendum):

1) Cap: "Redwood's aggregate liability and indemnity obligations for claims arising under this pilot order shall not exceed the total fees actually invoiced to Vector under the pilot order." (we'll define invoiced to exclude subsequent credits issued after final billing period).

2) Defense & settlement: Redwood will have lead defense control for third-party IP claims. Vector will have the right to approve any settlement that imposes monetary obligations > $0 on Vector or that seeks injunctive or equitable relief directly restricting Vector's pre-existing core product functionality; such approval will not be unreasonably withheld, delayed, or conditioned. If Vector withholds approval, the parties will cooperate in good faith; Redwood may continue defense at its cost.

3) OSS carveout: Claims arising solely from Vector's unmodified use of identified third-party OSS (list to be provided and agreed at signing) will be excluded from Redwood indemnity. Claims related to the model's outputs or Redwood-managed artifacts remain within scope.

4) Proof of insurance: Redwood will provide certificate of insurance for the pilot upon request. No escrow for pilot.

If that reads ok, Marco / Lydia — please confirm and we will send a one-paragraph addendum and updated order form via DocuSign. Jordan / Marissa — if you both sign off, I'll trigger DocuSign and update the HubSpot deal stage.

Best,
Kimberly
